_comment: Feature 56 Frond extensibility scope contract, governed by ADR-0052.
Class calls are process-global; instance calls are instance-local.
The same four pure in-memory cases run in all four frameworks without mocks.
ADR-0106: class GLOBALS are read live at render time, so a class global reaches an engine that
already exists (response.render's), and the auto-wired i18n t() is a class global taking a params map.
Those cases render a real template through a real route and the real request path in each framework.

invariants.rule: A class registration is inherited by every Frond instance constructed afterward.
invariants.why: Applications need one explicit startup-level mechanism for process-wide Frond extensions.

invariants.rule: An instance filter registration affects that Frond instance only.
invariants.why: An instance call must not contaminate later renderers or tests.
cases: instance filter registration is instance local

invariants.rule: An instance global registration affects that Frond instance only.
invariants.why: Per-renderer values must not become process-global state.
cases: instance global registration is instance local

invariants.rule: An instance test registration affects that Frond instance only.
invariants.why: Custom predicates must obey the same scope rule as filters and globals.
cases: instance test registration is instance local

invariants.rule: A class global reaches every template response.render renders afterwards, whether it was registered before or after the response engine was built; zero-argument and parameterised callables included.
invariants.why: Engines copied class globals at construction, so a registration after the first render never reached a page (all four).
cases: class global registered before first render reaches render
class global registered after first render reaches render
zero arg class global registered after first render is called
callable class global registered after first render is called

invariants.rule: With class globals read live, an instance global still never leaks into another engine, and it overrides a class global of the same name on its own engine only.
invariants.why: The live class layer must not weaken ADR-0052's instance isolation.
cases: instance global on another engine does not leak into render

invariants.rule: When locale files exist the framework registers t() as a class global that response.render templates can call as t("key") and t("key", {params}), whenever the response engine was built.
invariants.why: Ruby and Node registered t() where response.render never looked, and Python/Ruby rejected a params map.
cases: auto wired t translates a key
auto wired t accepts a params map
auto wired t reaches every engine
auto wired t registered after first render reaches render
